specialists_or_stages: mantis-researcher (stage 5, inline; wave-1 triage + wave-2 deep audit run as 6 per-component sweeps plus 2 cross-component sweeps)
mantis-review (stage 7, inline; 13 negative constraints applied per finding)
architecture.fell_back_and_why: Fan-out was attempted first and refused by the harness, not declined by me. The first delegation (stage 2, @mantis-architecture) and an immediate one-call probe both returned 'Concurrent subagent limit reached. You can run 20 subagents at once. Do not retry.' with zero subagents spawned by this session, so the pool was already saturated from outside it. mantis-researcher's wave-based swarm (SKILL.md step 2) and mantis-review's independent fresh-context validation were therefore run inline in this single context. Two properties of the design are consequently weakened and are stated rather than papered over: the reviewer was not context-independent of the researcher (the same context produced and then adversarially re-checked each claim against the pinned source), and no per-subagent transcripts exist, which degraded stage 13. Everything else in the pipeline ran as specified.

stages_run: mantis-meta-agent (pass lifecycle: sync skipped for vcs_type=none, fresh VCS detect, PIN immutable snapshot, record state)
stages_skipped: mantis-history (stage 0) - the target has no VCS: git rev-parse fails and there is no .hg/.repo/.svn, so vcs_type resolves to 'none' and there is no history to mine for past vulnerabilities. Nothing offline could substitute.

mantis-structural-index (stage 0.5) - optional and HINT-only by its own SKILL.md ('never gates findings and degrades gracefully to an empty index (grep fallback)'). Skipped deliberately: at 60 files and ~4,500 lines the mandated repo-wide grep floor is already exhaustive, so an index could only have reordered work it could not change.

mantis-summarize (stage 1) - skipped by the skill's own rule, not by choice. In PINNED mode mantis-summarize/SKILL.md:97-98 and :165-168 forbid writing mantis-summary.md ('Do NOT write any mantis-summary.md files in PINNED mode'). PINNED mode was selected precisely so the read-only constraint on TARGET would hold, since MODE-OFF would have written a summary file into each source directory.

mantis-reproduce (stage 9) - ran only at tier 1 and is otherwise skipped. The functional and full-service tiers need dependencies that cannot be installed offline: pydantic, redis, psycopg, openai and jsonschema are all absent from the interpreter, no node_modules exist for hono/zod/jose or @pulumi/aws, and there is no Android SDK, no Postgres, no Redis and no AWS. Four pure-function micro-harnesses were transplanted verbatim into a private shadow directory and executed, confirming: scrubNotes passes event-handler XSS payloads through byte-for-byte, cache.listKey collides across roles, the settlement HMAC with its empty default secret accepts a forged payout, and limits.replay_slot collides across principals. Every other finding is statically confirmed against the pinned snapshot and none is reported as reproduced.

mantis-patch (stage 11) - skipped because the task forbids modifying TARGET and the pinned snapshot is chmod a-w. No patch was generated or applied, so no finding carries a patch_status, a reattack_status or a VERIFIED_SECURE verdict.
mantis-advise / mantis-pipeline-adapter - not pipeline stages; they are guidance documents for building custom harnesses.

snapshot.note: MANTIS's opt-in snapshot model was enabled so every stage reads an immutable, chmod a-w copy under mantis-run2/.mantis_snapshots/pass_1 and TARGET is never written. The id follows the ladder's no-VCS tier: content:<sha256 over every file in the pinned copy>.

provenance.review_constraint_mapping: FP-01..FP-13 are MANTIS's own 13 negative constraints from mantis-review/SKILL.md step 3, in order: FP-01 ignore_hypothetical_misuse, FP-02 ignore_missing_hygiene, FP-03 require_strict_reproducibility, FP-04 avoid_pedantic_linting, FP-05 no_security_flaw_stretching, FP-06 evaluate_questionable_file_paths, FP-07 ignore_resource_exhaustion_dos, FP-08 intrinsic_security_flaws, FP-09 verify_mitigations_pragmatically, FP-10 refine_code_paths_strictly, FP-11 ignore_simd_vector_padding, FP-12 ensure_source_code_coherence, FP-13 verify_attacker_control_of_source. Answer semantics: DOES_NOT_HOLD = the rule gives no ground to discard the finding (MANTIS outcome PASS); HOLDS = the rule fires (MANTIS outcome FAIL), which under the skill forces status FALSE_POSITIVE - so HOLDS never appears on a reported finding and instead shows up as a ruled_out entry; UNKNOWN and NOT_APPLICABLE carry their MANTIS meanings and always carry a reason. FP-08 is the one non-disqualifying rule (it rescues intrinsic flaws with no live caller); DOES_NOT_HOLD on FP-08 means the rescue applies. FP-11 is NOT_APPLICABLE everywhere: this corpus contains no SIMD or vector code. FP-10 and FP-12 were enforced mechanically - every path and line in code_paths/applies_to was read under the pinned snapshot before it was written down, and code_paths carry only the lines where the construct takes effect.

ruled_out.assertion: Remote code execution via the operator-supplied `template` query parameter compiled with `new Function` in the print handler
ruled_out.killed_by: The mitigation was checked on its own terms and holds. printQuery is declared .strict() (workorders.ts:164-168) and hono's zValidator('query', ...) validates the whole query object - every parameter present on the URL, not only the declared ones - so a request carrying ?template=... fails validation with 400 before the handler runs, and c.req.query('template') at :185 can only ever be undefined. The DEFAULT_SHEET fallback (:162) is a fixed literal whose only interpolation is the runtime property read `wo.title`, which is substituted as a value and cannot inject code. The unescaped HTML output of render(wo) is reported separately as stored XSS.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection through the interpolated LIMIT/OFFSET in the work-order list query
ruled_out.killed_by: Both interpolated values are numbers by construction: page is Math.max(0, parseInt(...) || 0) and limit is Math.min(100, Math.max(1, parseInt(...) || 50)) (workorders.ts:50-51), so NaN and non-numeric input collapse to the defaults and no string reaches the SQL. Every other value in the statement is parameterised.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection through the f-string interpolated `reference` column in the ledger journal insert
ruled_out.killed_by: post_entry only accepts a LedgerEntry (ledger.py:54), and pydantic validates reference against the anchored pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9:_.\-]{1,64}$ on construction (schemas.py:16, :43). Quotes, semicolons, spaces and every other metacharacter are rejected, so no injectable value can reach line 81. All four remaining values are parameterised. Flagged as fragile - the safety depends entirely on a model constraint declared in a different module - but not exploitable as written.

ruled_out.assertion: SQL injection through the `partner_id` dbt var interpolated into the export model's WHERE clause
ruled_out.killed_by: The value is passed through modules.re.sub("[^a-z0-9-]", "", requested_partner | lower) at partner_extract.sql:16 before interpolation, which removes quotes and every other metacharacter. The var is also operator-supplied on the dbt command line (:11), not attacker-reachable.

ruled_out.assertion: WebView file-origin escalation via the allow_file_access intent extra enabling allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs
ruled_out.killed_by: No untrusted writer can set the extra. ReportWebViewActivity is android:exported="false" with no intent filter (AndroidManifest.xml:55-58), so no external app can start it, and neither in-app factory sets EXTRA_ALLOW_FILE_ACCESS (intentFor at :26-27, offlineIntent at :29-32). A repo-wide grep finds the constant only at its declaration (:24) and its read (:50). The rule 08 exception does not rescue it: the defect is a settings toggle, not an injection sink or hardcoded secret.

ruled_out.assertion: SessionStore.exportSessionForSupport leaks the full bearer token
ruled_out.killed_by: A repo-wide grep finds no call site; the surviving support sheet calls redactedSummary() instead (DeepLinkRouter.kt:96, SessionStore.kt:65). Reaching the token would require a caller that does not exist, which is the hypothetical-misuse case rule 01 excludes. Recommend deleting the function as hygiene, not as a finding.

ruled_out.assertion: createLegacyArchive provisions a fully public S3 bucket
ruled_out.killed_by: A repo-wide grep finds no caller: index.ts imports only createStorage (index.ts:7, :45) and the function is never referenced. No stack in this repository instantiates the bucket, so no resource with this policy exists. Distinguished from the settlement-worker IAM fallback, which IS instantiated on every deploy. Worth deleting, but not a live exposure.

ruled_out.assertion: grant_all_to_analysts grants ALL PRIVILEGES on relations and schemas to analyst_role
ruled_out.killed_by: A repo-wide grep finds no invocation; dbt_project.yml wires only apply_grants as a post-hook (:33, :41, :48). An unreferenced dbt macro emits no DDL. The macro's own comment marks it as superseded (:37-40).

ruled_out.assertion: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on the RAG service exposes authenticated responses to any origin
ruled_out.killed_by: The service is bearer-only: every route authorises from the Authorization header (app.py:71-78) and no endpoint reads a cookie, while cors_allow_credentials is False (settings.py:44) and no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials header is emitted (app.py:256-258). A wildcard origin without credentials does not let a foreign page attach the victim's authorisation, so there is no ambient-authority crossing. The comment at settings.py:42-43 was verified against the code rather than accepted.

ruled_out.assertion: Unsalted SHA-256 storage of RAG API keys and session tokens permits offline recovery
ruled_out.killed_by: Keys are secrets.token_urlsafe(32) (app.py:212, :230), i.e. 256 bits of CSPRNG output, so a digest without a salt or a work factor is not brute-forceable. Rule 04 excludes demanding extra paranoia around a correct use of a standard-library hash on a high-entropy input.

ruled_out.assertion: Caller-supplied `filters` in the RAG query can override the tenant or collection predicate
ruled_out.killed_by: The mitigation the comment claims is real. search copies the caller's filters into `where` and then overwrites both tenancy keys unconditionally (retriever.py:56-57), and only 'source_kind' is ever turned into an additional clause (:60-61); the SQL clause list is built from literals only (:59, :67). Extra filter keys become unused named parameters, and the explicit kwargs in dict(where, vector=..., k=...) (:72) win over any caller value of the same name.

ruled_out.assertion: The settlement notification hook is an SSRF sink because httpx follows redirects
ruled_out.killed_by: _notify is only ever called with settings.notify_url (handlers.py:73), which is server-authored configuration from an environment variable (settings.py:45-47). No attacker-controlled value reaches the hook_url parameter anywhere in the corpus, which is the trusted-origin case rule 13 marks as a false positive. The plaintext http:// scheme of the default is a hygiene item under rule 02.

ruled_out.assertion: tools.dispatch splats model-supplied keyword arguments into the tool function
ruled_out.killed_by: An unexpected keyword raises TypeError out of the request handler, which is an availability fault rather than a security boundary crossing: the registry resolves only two known functions (tools.py:91-94, :99) and no argument can select code. Rule 07 excludes reporting a function for missing input-shape limits when the module's purpose is not DoS defence. The genuine issue on this path - the unrestricted url argument - is reported separately.

ruled_out.assertion: The reports bucket public-access block leaves blockPublicPolicy and restrictPublicBuckets false
ruled_out.killed_by: No public policy is attached to that bucket: the only policy on it names the partner role as principal (storage.ts:114-132), and the bucket is served through CloudFront with Origin Access Control (edge.ts:199-203, :244). The setting removes a guardrail against a future mistake, which is the defence-in-depth case rule 02 excludes.

ruled_out.assertion: The WAF prefix rules protecting /ops/ and the reports /internal/ prefix are bypassable through path normalisation
ruled_out.killed_by: No concrete bypass could be demonstrated against the pinned snapshot. Both rules apply a URL_DECODE transformation on uriPath (edge.ts:172, :225), and the candidate evasions considered - case variation and duplicated separators - do not survive the case-sensitive S3 key lookup and the equally case-sensitive ALB path pattern (:139). Recording the residual concern that a path-prefix blocklist is the only control in front of the internal report objects; the missing OIDC action on the ALB's /internal/* rule is reported separately as a confirmed finding.

ruled_out.assertion: Private subnet CIDRs 10.1.0.0/20 and 10.1.16.0/20 fall outside the VPC CIDR 10.0.0.0/16
ruled_out.killed_by: Real defect but not a security one: for the second availability zone the computed blocks (network.ts:49, :61) lie outside args.cidr (index.ts:41), so AWS rejects the subnet at create time and the deploy fails loudly. It cannot produce a silently over-broad network.

findings.title: Production trusts unverified x-fieldops-* identity headers, granting anonymous admin
findings.evidence: config.ts:28 sets trustProxyIdentity to (NODE_ENV === 'production'). requireAuth (auth.ts:57-67) falls back to fromProxyHeaders when no bearer verifies, and fromProxyHeaders (auth.ts:45-54) builds the Actor straight out of the request headers x-fieldops-actor / -org / -role / -crews with no proof the request traversed the load balancer and no signature. The infrastructure side confirms the headers are not stripped: the ALB is created with dropInvalidHeaderFields:false (pulumi-platform/edge.ts:35) with the comment that the listener 'has to pass request headers through to the target group untouched', and the /api/* listener rule (edge.ts:93-98) forwards with no header-manipulation action. The ALB is internet-facing on 0.0.0.0/0:443 (network.ts:72-80).
findings.impact: Any internet client can send 'x-fieldops-role: admin' plus any org id and obtain a fully privileged actor on every /api/v1/* route: read and mutate any org's work orders, and satisfy canWriteSite() unconditionally (policy.ts:37-38). Complete authentication and tenancy bypass in production only.
findings.recommendation: Do not derive identity from request headers. Terminate mTLS identity into a signed, short-lived token, or have the ALB overwrite (not append) the x-fieldops-* headers and set dropInvalidHeaderFields:true; additionally bind the header path to the ALB's source security group.

triage.reason: no SIMD/vector routines anywhere in this corpus

ingress traced: HTTP request headers read at auth.ts:46-52 via c.req.raw.headers (auth.ts:60), reachable from the internet through the ALB listener rule at pulumi-platform/edge.ts:93 with dropInvalidHeaderFields:false at edge.ts:35

scope.established_by: config.trustProxyIdentity (fieldops-api/src/config.ts:28) enables the header path for NODE_ENV=production; index.ts:28 mounts requireAuth on /api/v1/*, so the construct takes effect on every authenticated route.
scope.narrowed_by: Inert outside production: trustProxyIdentity is false for any other NODE_ENV, so the fallback at auth.ts:59 is not entered.

findings.title: Legacy /files mount serves attachments through soft auth, allowing unauthenticated cross-org reads
findings.evidence: index.ts:28 applies requireAuth only to '/api/v1/*'. The same attachments router is mounted a second time at config.legacyFilesMount ('/files', config.ts:32) behind attachActor (index.ts:35-36), which by design lets the request through whether or not an actor resolves (auth.ts:74-78). The handlers then guard with 'if (actor && actor.orgId !== row.orgId)' (attachments.ts:80 and :97) - a check that is skipped entirely when actor is undefined. selectAttachment (attachments.ts:24-32) looks the row up by id alone, with no org predicate. The comment at attachments.ts:78-79 claims 'the grant rides on the link itself', but no signature, expiry or MAC is verified anywhere in the file.
findings.impact: An unauthenticated caller who knows or enumerates an attachment id reads its metadata (GET /files/:id) and streams its bytes (GET /files/:id/raw) regardless of which organisation owns it. Attachments are field photographs and signed customer paperwork.
findings.recommendation: Mount the legacy prefix behind requireAuth like the versioned path, and make the org check unconditional (deny when no actor). If pre-signed links are genuinely required, verify a real signature and expiry before serving bytes.

triage.reason: no SIMD/vector routines anywhere in this corpus
ingress is the unauthenticated HTTP path parameter at attachments.ts:74 and :93 (c.req.param('id')), reachable on the public /files prefix mounted at index.ts:36

scope.established_by: index.ts:35-36 mounts the attachments router under attachActor at the '/files' prefix; both read handlers inherit the optional-actor contract.
scope.narrowed_by: POST /files (upload, attachments.ts:38-66) is not exploitable the same way: it dereferences actor.orgId at line 62 and throws before writing when no actor is present.

findings.title: Session JWT signing key falls back to a hardcoded literal
findings.evidence: sessionSecret is env.SESSION_SECRET ?? 'local-development-session-key' (config.ts:23). That value is the HS256 key used both to mint (session.ts:9, :48-56) and to verify (auth.ts:20, :26-29) every session token. Nothing validates that the variable was supplied: there is no assertion, no startup check, and the API boots identically with or without it. The deployment code in this repository never sets SESSION_SECRET - a repo-wide grep for it matches only fieldops-api/src/config.ts:23.
findings.impact: If the environment variable is ever missing or empty in a deployed task, every session token is signed with a key published in this repository, so anyone can forge a token with role 'admin' for any org and bypass authentication entirely.
findings.recommendation: Fail closed at boot when SESSION_SECRET is absent, and reject keys shorter than 32 bytes. Source the key from Secrets Manager (the API task role already has secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on fieldops/api/*, pulumi-platform/iam.ts:22-26).

triage.reason: MANTIS rule 08 keeps a hardcoded static secret valid on its own terms, independent of whether a deployment currently overrides it
no SIMD/vector routines anywhere in this corpus
rule 08 intrinsic-flaw exception: the defect is in the key material, not in a data flow from an untrusted writer

scope.established_by: The '??' fallback at config.ts:23 makes the literal the effective key whenever env.SESSION_SECRET is unset or empty; both the signer and the verifier read that single export.

findings.title: Work-order list cache key omits the role/crew narrowing, leaking the full org board to techs
findings.class: cache key confusion / horizontal privilege escalation
findings.evidence: listKey builds 'wo:list:<orgId>:<status>:<page>' (cache.ts:11-13) - org, status tab and page only. The list handler computes the crew narrowing AFTER the cache lookup: it reads the cache at workorders.ts:53-58 and only then calls visibleCrewFilter(actor) at :60, which returns actor.crewIds for role 'tech' and null (no narrowing) for dispatcher/manager (policy.ts:47-50). The narrowed and unnarrowed responses are stored under the identical key at :76. A tier-1 harness transplanting listKey verbatim confirms the collision: listKey('org-4','scheduled',0) is byte-identical for a tech and for a dispatcher.
findings.impact: Whichever role populates the cache first serves every other role for the TTL (45 s by default, config.ts:38). When a dispatcher or manager populates it, a tech receives the whole organisation's board including work orders for crews they are not on - the exact rows visibleCrewFilter exists to withhold. It also leaks between techs on different crews.
findings.recommendation: Include every input to the authorisation decision in the cache key (role plus a stable hash of the crew filter), or cache only after narrowing and key by the narrowed predicate.

triage.reason: deterministic, not timing-dependent: the collision is reproduced by a pure-function harness over cache.ts:11
no SIMD/vector routines anywhere in this corpus
ingress is the authenticated request's own actor claims (workorders.ts:45) plus the attacker-chosen status/page query params validated at workorders.ts:44-51

scope.established_by: cache.listKey (cache.ts:11) defines the key space; workorders.ts:53 and :76 are the only read and write sites, both on the authenticated list route.
scope.narrowed_by: Bounded by the TTL at config.ts:38 and flushed per org on any write (cache.invalidateOrg, cache.ts:30, called at workorders.ts:104 and :154).

findings.title: Stored XSS in the printable work-order sheet: title and notes are emitted unescaped
findings.evidence:
The print handler escapes wo.id, wo.title, wo.siteId and wo.status where it uses escapeHtml (workorders.ts:189, :192, :194, :195) but emits two attacker-controlled fields raw: render(wo) at :191 expands the default template '

${wo.title}

' (:162) with no escaping, and ${wo.notes} at :197 is interpolated directly. title is stored with no sanitisation at all (createBody z.string().min(1).max(200), :27, inserted at :101). notes passes only scrubNotes (policy.ts:57-62), a three-pattern blocklist that strips
findings.impact: Any actor who can create or patch a work order in an org stores script that runs in the browser of every user who opens that order's print sheet, in the API's own origin: session theft, and write actions replayed as the viewer (dispatcher or manager).
findings.recommendation: Escape both fields with escapeHtml at :191 and :197, and replace the scrubNotes blocklist with an allowlisting sanitiser or with contextual output encoding at every render site.

triage.reason: the scrubNotes mitigation was evaluated on its own terms and measured to fail: it is a three-pattern blocklist with no event-handler coverage
no SIMD/vector routines anywhere in this corpus
ingress: the JSON body fields title/notes at workorders.ts:87 and :114, written to the database at :101 and :139 by any authenticated actor in the org

scope.established_by: The two unescaped interpolations at workorders.ts:191 and :197 in the html response returned by c.html at :200; the stored values originate at the create (:101) and patch (:139) handlers.
scope.narrowed_by: escapeHtml is applied to the other four interpolations in the same template, so only title and notes carry the defect.

findings.title: PATCH /workorders/:id enforces no role and no site clearance, unlike the create path
findings.evidence: The create handler runs both checks: sameOrgSite then canWriteSite (workorders.ts:89-94). The patch handler checks only that the row belongs to the actor's org (:123) and, when siteId changes, only sameOrgSite (:133) - canWriteSite is never called on the update path. There is no role gate either: requireRole exists (auth.ts:81-89) but a repo-wide grep finds no call site, so the router is reachable by role 'tech'. Every mutable column is therefore writable by any authenticated member of the org: site_id (:136), title (:138), notes (:139), crew_id (:140) and status (:141).
findings.impact: A technician can move any work order in the organisation onto a site their crew is not cleared for, reassign it to another crew, and close or reopen it - the authorisation that canWriteSite provides on create is simply absent on update.
findings.recommendation: Apply canWriteSite to the patch path (both to the existing site and to any new siteId), and gate crew_id and status transitions behind requireRole('dispatcher','manager','admin').

triage.reason: no SIMD/vector routines anywhere in this corpus
ingress: the JSON body validated at workorders.ts:113-114 and the path parameter at :115, supplied by any authenticated tech

scope.established_by: The patch route registered at workorders.ts:112 under the requireAuth mount (index.ts:28-29); the missing call is to policy.canWriteSite defined at policy.ts:36.
scope.narrowed_by: Cross-org writes are still blocked by the org check at workorders.ts:123 and by sameOrgSite at :133.

findings.title: The /session/token password grant repeats the credential check without the login rate limiter
findings.evidence: index.ts:24 attaches loginLimiter to exactly one path: '/api/v1/session/login'. The /token route mounted with the same router (index.ts:25) performs an identical email+password verification for grantType='password' (session.ts:87-95) and is not covered by any limiter. Both call the same findPrincipal and passwordMatches. The refresh branch (:98-107) is likewise unlimited and matches the token by plaintext equality with no rotation or single-use marking.
findings.impact: The 8-attempts-per-minute guard on the sign-in form (config.ts:40) is bypassed by pointing the same credential stuffing at /api/v1/session/token, which returns the same 401/200 oracle without throttling.
findings.recommendation: Attach the limiter to the whole unauthenticated session surface (login, token and recover) rather than to a single path, and key it per account as well as per client address.

triage.reason: rule 07's exception applies: the primary stated purpose of rateLimit.ts is brute-force defence ('Brute-force guard for the interactive sign-in form', rateLimit.ts:42)
no SIMD/vector routines anywhere in this corpus
ingress: unauthenticated JSON body at session.ts:85

scope.established_by: The limiter mount at index.ts:24 is path-scoped to /login; session.ts:84 and :111 are siblings on the same public router mounted at index.ts:25.

findings.title: Analytics read replica is publicly accessible and the shared DB security group is opened to 0.0.0.0/0
findings.evidence: The replica is created with publiclyAccessible:true (data.ts:64) inside a subnet group built from network.publicSubnetIds (:54-57), which are the subnets with mapPublicIpOnLaunch:true routed to the internet gateway (network.ts:47-57, :30-33). It then attaches network.dbSecurityGroup (:63) and, unconditionally, adds an ingress rule for tcp/5432 from cidrIpv4 '0.0.0.0/0' (:71-78). The comment at :69-70 states this is deliberate because the BI vendor's egress list is unreliable. The same security group is the primary's (data.ts:41) and was created with the description 'Postgres - application tier only' and a single app-tier ingress (network.ts:97-109); this rule silently negates that.
findings.impact: The read replica carries a full copy of the production work-order and principal data and is reachable from the whole internet on the Postgres port, leaving password guessing against the 'fieldops' master user as the only remaining control. The same rule also removes the network boundary in front of the primary for anything already inside the VPC.
findings.recommendation: Delete the 0.0.0.0/0 rule; place the replica in the private subnets with publiclyAccessible:false and reach it over PrivateLink or a peered VPC. If the BI vendor must connect over the internet, terminate it on a dedicated proxy with its own security group.

triage.reason: not a missing-header/hygiene item: this creates a reachable listening service on the public internet
no SIMD/vector routines anywhere in this corpus
ingress: any internet host, admitted by the security group rule declared at data.ts:71-78

scope.established_by: createDataTier is invoked once per stack from index.ts:64-69, so the rule is created in every environment including prod (Pulumi.prod.yaml:4).

findings.title: settlement-worker's task role falls through to an Allow */* bootstrap policy
findings.evidence: SERVICES lists four workloads (iam.ts:50-55) including 'settlement-worker', but SERVICE_POLICIES (iam.ts:15-42) defines entries for only three: fieldops-api, reports-renderer and warehouse-loader. The loop resolves 'const statements = SERVICE_POLICIES[service] ?? BOOTSTRAP_STATEMENTS' (:80), and BOOTSTRAP_STATEMENTS is a single { Effect:'Allow', Action:'*', Resource:'*' } (iam.ts:45-47). The role is then created with that policy attached (:82-85). Nothing in the file warns, fails, or logs when a service misses its entry.
findings.impact: The settlement worker task - a Redis consumer that moves money - runs with unrestricted AWS administrator permissions in every environment. Anyone who achieves code execution in that container (the deserialisation and replay defects in settlement-worker make that a live concern) owns the whole account: all buckets, all databases, all IAM.
findings.recommendation: Give settlement-worker an explicit least-privilege entry and make the fallback fail closed - throw on a missing SERVICE_POLICIES entry instead of substituting an administrator policy. Delete BOOTSTRAP_STATEMENTS.

triage.reason: an Allow */* policy is an intrinsic defect in this module's own logic
no SIMD/vector routines anywhere in this corpus
rule 08 intrinsic-flaw exception; no untrusted data flow is required

scope.established_by: The '??' fallback at iam.ts:80 inside the loop over SERVICES (iam.ts:65) is what attaches the wildcard policy; createRoles is called once per stack at index.ts:43.
scope.narrowed_by: Only settlement-worker takes the fallback today; the other three entries in SERVICES resolve to real policies.

findings.title: Staging export bucket is world-readable while being loaded with replicated production objects
findings.evidence: Two staging settings compose into a public disclosure. publicExports:'true' (Pulumi.staging.yaml:9) is read at index.ts:13 and passed to createStorage (:45-50). Inside, every BucketPublicAccessBlock field is set to !args.publicExports, i.e. all four guards become false (storage.ts:42-48), and a bucket policy with Principal '*' and s3:GetObject on '<arn>/*' is attached (:50-67).
